correctness.rationale: F_X=Z³,F_Y=X³,F_Z=Y³ are never simultaneously zero in projective space. On each tangent in characteristic 3 the quadratic Taylor term vanishes; the residual fourth point is Phi(P), on the tangent since the tangent substitution equals F(P)^3. Degree-four Bézout handles fixed/nonfixed cases, and precludes two distinct double contacts. Fixed-point coordinates reduce reversibly to u^28+u^21+1 using u^91=1; independently factored over F3 with degrees 1,3,6×4, verified g|(u^91-1), and gcd(g,g')=1. Frobenius-equivariant tangent map gives bitangent field counts and reduced zeta for every n; finite extension checks alone are not used as proof.
residual_risks: Finite independent checks corroborate only their stated bounded domain; the universal claim depends on reconstructed analytic proof.
